policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'And when Peter was come up' renders either the connective de ('and') or kai equally; no wording distinguishes hote de from Kai hote.
Both spellings are rendered 'Jerusalem'; the English cannot distinguish Ierousalem from Hierosoluma.

ASV 'Thou wentest in ... and didst eat' is second person singular, excluding r03 (eiselthen ... sunephagen, third person). The remaining readings differ only in word order, which the English does not register.
ASV 'But Peter began' leaves the article before the proper name untranslatable either way; English supplies no equivalent of ho.
ASV 'And I heard also a voice' renders the adjunctive kai with 'also'; the reading omitting kai leaves that word unaccounted for.
ASV 'nothing common or unclean hath ever entered' renders the pan ... oudepote idiom and the simple negative alike; no English word answers to or excludes pan.

ASV 'a voice answered the second time out of heaven' has no dative 'me', excluding r02 (moi phone). The remaining two differ only in the order of phone and ek deuterou, which the English does not show.
ASV 'all were drawn up again' renders either order of anespasthe and palin.
ASV 'the house in which we were' is first person plural (emen); emen ('I was') would have given 'in which I was'.
ASV 'the Spirit bade me go' renders either order of to pneuma and moi.
ASV 'making no distinction' renders the active diakrinanta (to discriminate); the middle diakrinomenon yields the sense 'nothing doubting', which the ASV does not give.
ASV 'and he told us' renders either connective de or te; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV 'and saying, Send to Joppa' has no indirect object; the added auto would have been rendered 'saying unto him'.
ASV 'Send to Joppa, and fetch Simon' has no object 'men'; the added andras would have given 'Send men to Joppa'.
The presence or absence of the article is not registered in ASV 'the word of the Lord'; the mapped note ('Or, with') is an alternative_rendering about the preposition and decides no reading.
ASV 'who was I, that I could withstand God?' renders no connective at ego; the added de leaves no English trace.
ASV 'glorified God' renders the aorist edoxasan and the imperfect edoxazon alike.
ASV 'Then to the Gentiles also' renders ara with 'Then'; the emphatic particle ge is regularly left untranslated and its presence cannot be read off the English.
ASV 'hath God granted repentance unto life' renders either order of eis zoen and edoken.
ASV 'when they were come to Antioch' renders the simple elthontes; the compound eiselthontes is rendered 'entered into' in this same chapter (v. 12, 'we entered into the man's house').
ASV 'spake unto the Greeks also' renders the adjunctive kai with 'also'; the reading omitting kai leaves that word unaccounted for.

ASV text reads 'the Greeks' (Hellenas) and its mapped textual_variant note puts the other reading in the margin: 'Many ancient authorities read Grecian Jews' — the ASV rendering of Hellenistas, as at 6:1.
ASV 'the hand of the Lord' does not register the presence or absence of the Greek article.
ASV 'the church which was in Jerusalem' renders the attributive article with or without ouses; 'which was' is required in English either way.
Both spellings are rendered 'Jerusalem'; the English cannot distinguish Ierousalem from Hierosolumois.
ASV 'they sent forth Barnabas as far as Antioch' has no verb answering to dielthein; that infinitive would have been rendered 'to go as far as Antioch'.
ASV 'with purpose of heart' does not register the article before kardias; the mapped note bears on the construal of en to kurio, not on this article.

The mapped textual_variant note assigns the en reading to the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read that they would cleave unto the purpose of their heart in the Lord' — so the ASV text 'cleave unto the Lord' follows prosmenein without en.
ASV 'And he went forth to Tarsus' keeps the pronominal subject; the added ho Barnabas would have been rendered 'Barnabas went forth'.
English requires an object for 'brought', so 'he brought him unto Antioch' stands whether or not auton is read, and the ASV marks no supply here.
ASV 'that even for a whole year they were gathered together' renders the adjunctive kai with 'even'; the accusative autous without kai leaves that word unaccounted for.

The ASV note 'Greek in.' reports the preposition en behind the rendering 'gathered together with the church'; the reading omitting en leaves the bare dative, which the note would have no occasion to gloss.
ASV 'called Christians first in Antioch' renders protos and proton alike.
ASV 'a great famine' renders either gender of the adjective with limon.
ASV 'which came to pass in the days of Claudius' has no 'also'; the ASV renders adjunctive kai in this chapter ('also' vv. 7, 20; 'even' v. 26), so hostis kai would have shown.
ASV 'in the days of Claudius' has no 'Caesar'; the added Kaisaros would have been rendered.
